stories.headline: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.title: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.summary: New York, Oct 15 : A teenager was arrested for allegedly plotting to carry out a "mass shooting" at a Hindu place of worship in the US state of Illinois, with investigators recovering a manifesto expressing white supremacist ideology and references to violence against people of Indian descent. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine village was arrested on October 11 and charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon. According to investigators, the youth had tried to open fire "potentially targeting" the place of worship in the Aurora city in Illinois, but his gun jammed, forcing him to drive back home, a move that prevented a mass murder. The specific intended location has not been disclosed by the authorities. Palatine Police detectives examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)", which contained "statements expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence directed toward individuals of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent". Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning to carry out the attack on October 11. "However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation," police said on Wednesday. The Consulate General of India in Chicago said it appreciated the timely action by law enforcement authorities and was in touch with members of the Indian diaspora while closely monitoring developments. The arrest comes amid celebrations of Hindu festivals, including Navaratri and Durga Puja, and just two weeks after the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, Ohio, was vandalised. On October 11, the Palatine Police Department was contacted by the Mount Prospect Police Department regarding information it had received about a potential mass shooting. The information originated from an individual who reported receiving concerning electronic communications from Paporakis. According to a report by NBC Chicago, Paporakis had worked as a cashier at fast-food restaurant Taco Bell and had plotted to carry out a "mass shooting of Indian people" at a Hindu temple in Aurora. He drove to the temple last Sunday "decked out for war". The day he chose to carry out the carnage at the sprawling place of worship was filled with people. He was "one malfunctioning rifle away from becoming a mass shooter". Paporakis showed up "to kill a significant number of Indians", the report said, quoting police. Investigators said he had a "modified AR-style rifle and 300 rounds of ammo, enough to fill ten magazines for reloading, along with body armour, gasoline cans" and an assortment of Hakenkreuz (hooked cross used by Nazis), the report said. Paporakis allegedly drove from his mother's home in Palatine to the Aurora temple. Authorities said that "he tried to open fire but the gun jammed, so he drove home". There he "searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam his gun and called a colleague, informing them of (his) intent to carry out a mass shooting". The co-worker then notified the police, informing them of the plot, and Paporakis was arrested Sunday before he could return to the temple. The youth was arrested as he was leaving his residence following a coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect police departments. Paporakis has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday at the Cook County Third Municipal District Courthouse in Rolling Meadows, where a judge ordered him detained. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 30. According to investigators, Paporakis "expressed pleasure calling himself a sociopathic white supremacist Neo-Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day". In a social media post, the Hindu American Foundation commended law enforcement for swift action. "We also urge the community to stay vigilant and report any potential threat. Every community deserves to worship without fear," it said. The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said the "disturbing plot" comes as Hindus gather in large numbers to celebrate Navratri, and just two weeks after an attack on a temple in Ohio. "Hindu temples and all houses of worship must be sanctuaries of peace, prayer, and solace - NEVER targets of hate, violence, or terror. We thank law enforcement for their swift action in averting what could have been an unspeakable tragedy. "We urge elected officials and law enforcement agencies to take the growing threats against Hindu places of worship seriously, strengthen protections, and unequivocally condemn Hinduphobia," it said in a social media post. The group called on temples and community organisations to review their security measures, remain vigilant, and promptly report suspicious activity. "The freedom to worship without fear is a fundamental American right. It must be protected," it said. Police said they were working with the FBI as the investigation continued, including a review of possible additional charges. Authorities have not identified any known ongoing threat to the public associated with the incident. "The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated... Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said. FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen said the agency aggressively works alongside its local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies. article_sentences: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar apologised to the Supreme Court while defending transport curbs during the October 10 protest.
The contempt case will test whether public-order measures breached the court's direction against completely suspending services.

Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar has told the Supreme Court that timely, proportionate and lawful police measures helped avert a major public order situation during protests in the national capital on October 10.

Kumar tendered an unconditional and unqualified apology in a contempt case concerning the alleged violation of the court’s direction against a complete suspension of Metro and train services during the protest.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi is scheduled to hear the matter on Thursday.

In an affidavit filed in the Supreme Court, Kumar said the preventive measures taken after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called the protest were based on intelligence inputs and an assessment of the prevailing and rapidly changing situation on the ground.
He referred to steps taken by the police administration, including the regulation of Delhi Metro services.
“These measures were directed towards maintaining peace and tranquillity and preventing any disturbance of public order in the national capital,” he said.
The commissioner said the police’s efforts and actions should be viewed in the context of Delhi being the national capital, with its particular sensitivities.

“No police administration can permit any breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, destruction of public and private property, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent events of October 6, 7 and 8,” the affidavit said.
“Notwithstanding the bona fide efforts of the police administration, an incorrect narrative is being sought to be propagated regarding the actions taken by it,” it added.

The affidavit was filed in the contempt case over the alleged violation of the Supreme Court’s direction to ensure there was no “complete prohibition” on Metro and train services in Delhi because of the October 10 protest.

stories.title: Supreme Court bars automatic reservation benefits after conversion to Islam

article_sentences: The Supreme Court upheld the Madras High Court ruling against automatic reservation after conversion to Islam.
The judgment clarifies that pre-conversion caste status cannot determine post-conversion quota eligibility.
The Supreme Court has ruled that Hindus from backward classes cannot continue to claim reservation benefits linked to their previous social status after converting to Islam.
It said backwardness under an earlier social order could not automatically be carried forward after conversion.
The court also held that a person following a religion other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism could not be treated as a member of a Scheduled Caste.
It upheld a Madras High Court ruling that conversion to Islam alone did not entitle a person to reservation under Tamil Nadu's Backward Class (Muslim) category.
A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's appeal against the high court order.
The high court had quashed a state government notification granting reservation benefits to people who had converted to Islam.
The Supreme Court said the high court order did not require its interference.

"No statutory benefit, protection, reservation, or other entitlement under Article 16(4) of the Constitution, the enjoyment of which is predicated upon a particular Hindu social order, can be claimed or extended merely on the basis of such antecedent membership after the person has converted to Islam, Christianity, or any other non-Hindu social order," the bench held.

It said a person who converts from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim reservation under Article 16(4) merely on the basis of the social backwardness linked to the person's status before conversion.

"A backwardness suffered in the antecedent social order cannot by itself be carried forward so as to confer upon him the status of a backward class in the region to which he has converted," the court said.

stories.summary: Shares of IDBI Bank fell over 7% to Rs 83.87 on Thursday, a day after surging nearly 13% following the Union Cabinet’s approval of Fairfax’s acquisition of a 60.72% stake in the lender. The decline comes amid profit-booking after the stock’s sharp rally on the long-awaited privatisation development.The stock had climbed to Rs 93.60 on Wednesday, its highest level in nearly two weeks, taking IDBI Bank’s market capitalisation above Rs 1 lakh crore. The rally followed the Cabinet’s approval of the sale of the government’s and LIC’s combined stake to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ subsidiary, M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., for Rs 52,878.08 crore.Also Read |Redington could gain as memory shortage reshapes ICT distribution; brokerage sees 20% upsideFairfax deal closes a long chapter for IDBI BankThe deal marks a major step in the lender’s transformation after years of financial stress. Fairfax’s bid of Rs 81 per share was above the Rs 75.99 average fair valuation arrived at by two independent professional valuation agencies.The government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank, while LIC will hold 19% after the transaction. The successful bidder will also have to go through the RBI’s ‘fit & proper’ assessment and secure other regulatory approvals before the deal is completed.The transaction is expected to become the largest foreign direct investment in India’s financial sector, according to Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 9,513 crore in FY26, while its total business rose 18% year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of September 30. Its latest quarterly business update showed deposits rising 17% to Rs 3.56 lakh crore and net advances growing 18% to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.With the privatisation now moving ahead, the next phase will be about what Fairfax does with the bank. The challenge will be to take a lender that has repaired its balance sheet and make it more competitive in the private banking space. stories.headline: India To Add Record 70 GW+ Power Capacity In FY27, Minister Calls For AI-Led Solutions
stories.title: India To Add Record 70 GW+ Power Capacity In FY27, Minister Calls For AI-Led Solutions
stories.summary: India is likely to add more than 70 GW of power generation capacity in 2026-27, the highest addition in a single year, said Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs Manohar Lal. Sharing these estimages at an inaugural session of the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) two-day international conference-cum-exhibition on, “Making Indian Power Sector AI-Enabled”, held virtually, Manohar Lal spoke about the need to make India’s power sector more intelligent. The event was held at the Manekshaw Centre in New Delhi. At the event, Manohar Lal emphasised that building a large and complex power system in the future would require not only producing more electricity but also managing it intelligently. He added that India’s installed power generation capacity had reached about 555 GW and that the country now needed to build a system capable of anticipating electricity demand. He also stressed the importance of better integrating renewable energy and energy storage, while ensuring an uninterrupted and affordable power supply for consumers. Lal called AI both a resource and a solution. According to him, AI can help forecast generation more accurately, improve grid management, plan maintenance in advance and detect power outages early. He said the sector must move from a reactive system to a predictive and proactive one, with attention to power data security and the responsible use of AI. Background The conference was being held on CEA’s 53rd Foundation Day. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, who also addressed the event virtually, said India had over 305 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, accounting for close to 55% of its total installed capacity of 554.5 GW. He said the key question was how intelligently India could integrate, transmit, dispatch and consume clean energy. AI, he added, could improve renewable energy forecasting, support real-time grid balancing, optimise storage, reduce curtailment and help identify congestion in the network. “AI can help us convert data into intelligence, intelligence into timely decisions and decisions into better outcomes,” he said. He added that human oversight and accountability must remain central to critical grid operations and that India should develop AI solutions suited to Indian conditions and extend them to other emerging economies. September 2026: India Crosses 308 GW of Non-Fossil Capacity Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy Shripad Yesso Naik said India had reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, more than five years ahead of its 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) timeline. article_sentences: The India Meteorological Department has declared that the north-east monsoon has established over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, South Interior Karnataka, and Kerala and Mahe with effect from today (October 15, Thursday).
Seasonal rainfall has begun over these notified areas even as the IMD announced that the preceding south-west monsoon (June to September) has withdrawn from the entire country as on date.
The four-month season has ended in a deficit for the South Peninsula.
On Thursday, a facilitating upper-air cyclonic circulation lay over south Coastal Tamil Nadu and in the lower levels of the atmosphere to bring in the north-east monsoon.

Easterly to north-easterly winds have set in over southern peninsular India as well as south, central and adjoining north-west Bay of Bengal along a trough adjacent to the east coast, to satisfy required parameters for declaring the arrival of the season.
Fairly widespread rainfall occurred over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, and adjoining areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Rayalaseema since Wednesday.

article_sentences: Raipur: India will look to majorly refine their T20 game when the era of new captain Smriti Mandhana begins with a three-match series against a zealful Zimbabwe here on Friday.
It will be the first time India and Zimbabwe face each other in a bilateral series.
India recently reaffirmed their dominance at the Asian level but they remain very much a work in progress in international cricket, especially in the shortest format.
The back-to-back premature exits in the T20 World Cup have exposed chinks in their armour.
India need improvement in all three departments of the game if they are to consistently challenge the likes of Australia.
India won a path-breaking ODI World Cup at home last year but lifting the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy at home early next year would be a tougher task.
On the batting front, the team is struggling to maintain momentum in the middle overs following the flying starts provided by Mandhana and Shafali Verma.
The number three spot has become a case of musical chairs and the form of Mandhana's predecessor, Harmanpreet Kaur, has been a concern for a while.
Now playing as a specialist batter in the side, Harmanpreet will be under more pressure to deliver.
India also need to groom more power hitters to support Richa Ghosh in the lower-order.
The fielding has let the team down on a number of occasions and needs significant improvement.
In the bowling department, the recent rise of Nandni Sharma has been a big positive but overall the pace attack needs more potency to strike regularly in all phases of the game.
